## 0bc8666b7693

**Concrete untaught shortcut.** In 400 production draws (100 seeds for each of
`plain`, `big_shape`, `dup_color`, and `decoy_one`), every legend-named color had
exactly one connected outside component. Therefore a learner can use only the
largest connected component for each color instead of the canonical rule's
actual behavior: aggregate *all* outside cells of that color before
normalization and 3x3 windowing.

`checks/audit/0bc8666b7693/multi_component_input.json` is a lawful accepted
counterexample made by adding one isolated color-8 cell to seed 0. `self_check`
returns `[]`; the supported canonical Racket application succeeds and exactly
matches the generator mirror, but differs from the retained
largest-component rival in `checks/audit/0bc8666b7693/rival_output.json`.
Evidence and construction details are in `checks/audit/0bc8666b7693/probe.json`,
`racket.json`, and `census.json`. The application records generator SHA-256
`a7cf2063fe784246cbea5fbb91b14706ced35ddc2106cc21fabfc61129189bcd` and rule
hash `5722ad1cca1e`. A cheap repair would occasionally split one named color
across two separated components and declare/test the largest-component rival.
No audit-target source was changed.
